hook_text: Can you write your name like a pharaoh and count like a scribe?
clip_script: Gqeberha, Eastern Cape. Learners write their names in hieroglyphics, inside an oval cartouche, like a pharaoh. More than seven hundred signs, for sounds and words, read again thanks to the Rosetta Stone. On the board: a lotus, three coils of rope, two heel bones and five strokes. That's 1,325, Egyptian style. And before dawn, the bright star Sirius rises in the east. For the Egyptians, it meant the flood was coming. Happy New Year!
visual_style: Whiteboard hieroglyphs forming a name in a cartouche, Egyptian number signs adding up, then Sirius rising over the Nile.
mood: Playful and clever, like cracking a secret code.
pacing: Three quick puzzles: write, count, stargaze.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your own name in hieroglyphics.
